stated: Labour will take preventative public health measures, ensuring the next generation can never legally buy cigarettes and integrating 'opt-out' smoking cessation interventions in hospitals. They will ban vapes from being branded and advertised to appeal to children, ban advertising junk food to children, and prohibit the sale of high-caffeine energy drinks to under-16s to tackle childhood obesity. The party will also strengthen online safety provisions, grant coroners more powers to access tech company information after a child's death, and reform gambling regulation to strengthen protections.

source.quote: Labour will ensure the next generation can never legally buy cigarettes and ensure all hospitals integrate ‘optout’ smoking cessation interventions into routine care. Labour will ban vapes from being branded and advertised to appeal to children to stop the next generation from becoming hooked on nicotine. Labour is committed to banning advertising junk food to children along with the sale of high-caffeine energy drinks to under-16s. Labour will build on the Online Safety Act, bringing forward provisions as quickly as possible, and explore further measures to keep everyone safe online, particularly when using social media. We will also give coroners more powers to access information held by technology companies after a child’s death. Labour is committed to reducing gambling-related harm. Recognising the evolution of the gambling landscape since 2005, Labour will reform gambling regulation, strengthening protections.

bearing_set.reason: Smoking ban, opt-out hospital cessation, and childhood obesity measures (junk food/energy drink/vape restrictions) directly reduce disease burden and NHS demand, earning a real verdict on healthcare access and capacity.

Online safety provisions, coroner powers over tech companies after a child's death, and gambling regulation reform directly address child protection from online harm and addiction-related harm, earning a real verdict on safety/justice.

The generational tobacco ban permanently restricts adults born after a set year from purchasing a legal product — a non-trivial restriction on personal liberty (civil freedoms indicator); coroner powers compelling tech-company data and online safety provisions also raise privacy and free-expression questions.

The generational cigarette ban permanently bars adults born after a cut-off date from ever legally purchasing a currently-legal product — a significant state restriction on adult bodily autonomy and consumer choice; advertising bans also restrict commercial speech, representing a non-negligible liberty cost even where the safety rationale is strong.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O3 (preventative health reducing NHS demand — clear mechanism) and O10 (generational tobacco ban is an unprecedented adult-choice restriction; advertising bans constrain commercial expression). Other potential spillovers — public finances via reduced smoking costs, inequality via health outcomes — are too diffuse and long-chain to clear the non-negligible bar at this stage.
